meaning:
1) to heap up, pile
2) to dwell
2a) (Qal)
2a1) to dwell
2a2) heap up (imp.)
Aramaic equivalent: dur (דּוּר "to dwell" H1753)

elsewhere.note: For a day in your courts is better than a thousand. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
Take the choice of the flock, and also a pile of wood for the bones under the cauldron. Make it boil well. Yes, let its bones be boiled within it.”
